channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: COP31: Vanuatu calls for UN climate summit reform, warns of backsliding
item.description: Vanuatu's Environment Minister Ralph Regenvanu has called for changes to the UN climate summit process, accusing a small group of countries of blocking progress and warning that COP31 risks reversing previous commitments.

item.title: Xi-Trump-Putin talks live: China, US and Russia leaders to hold landmark three-way meeting
item.description: The leaders of China, the US and Russia are set to hold a first-of-its-kind trilateral meeting on Thursday in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, on the sidelines of an APEC summit. The meeting between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, which Beijing said would involve "safeguarding world peace", has raised fears of a carve-up of the globe into "spheres of influence". Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.

item.title: WATCH: Animal rescuers describe cat rescue after Brooklyn building collapse
item.description: Rescuers are speaking out about the miraculous rescue of Isaac the cat after the deadly building collapse in Brooklyn.

item.title: 2026 CMA Awards open with moving Dolly Parton tribute from Lainey Wilson, Vince Gill
item.description: Parton died on Aug. 25 at the age of 80, following what her family said was a "brief" battle with cancer.

item.title: WATCH: NASA's Voyager 1 now a light-day away after 1977 launch
item.description: NASA launched its Voyager 1 space probe in 1977. It's made it more than 16 billion miles in space, marking the farthest any human made object has ever traveled.

item.title: WATCH: 'Looksmaxxing' influencer Clavicular indicted on rape charges
item.description: Braden Peters is accused of giving alcohol to a teen and sexually assaulting her at his family's Cape Cod home.

item.title: Anthropic announces price of $83 per share for IPO
item.description: Anthropic is set for a valuation well above $1 trillion.

item.title: Judge extends temporary restraining order that blocks construction of Trump's arch
item.description: The original order was set to expire on Thursday.

item.title: Anthropic IPO raises record $81.3 billion on strong AI demand
item.description: The five-year-old artificial intelligence powerhouse priced its initial public offering at $83 a share, shrugging off growing concern about a possible AI bubble and volatility in tech stocks.

item.title: 24-month matured Comté crowned world’s best cheese
item.description: With its nutty flavour and smooth, supple texture, it was aged for two years in a former military fortress in eastern France. Comté, an unpasteurised cow’s milk cheese from the Jura Mountains, has beaten more than five thousand challengers to the top prize at the prestigious annual 'World Cheese Awards'. FRANCE 24's Daniel Whittington has the story.

item.title: Paramedic responding to deadly accident discovers son is the victim
item.description: Logan Mumford, 28, died from his injuries after a car he had been working on fell on top of him, authorities said.

item.title: Inside Limoges City Hall devastated by arson attack
item.description: Work is underway to restore the city hall of Limoges, in central France, which was devastated by an arson attack during riots on October 17. More than €1.7 million has been raised through an online fundraising campaign in the wake of the disaster. Also on the show, the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI has finally been released, with gamers in Oceania among the first to get a taste of the latest instalment in the video game franchise.

item.title: After Nepal's epic flood, they're restoring their community ... and their lives
item.description: As the emergency response to the flood ends, aid workers turn to the hard work of rebuilding communities that lost everything. Many of those workers lost everything, too.

item.title: Children among hundreds of thousands of London transport users who may have been hit by data breach
item.description: Oyster photocard customers may have had their account details compromised after "suspicious activity" was detected, Transport for London (TfL) said.

item.title: Crimea bridge strike: Fact-checking fake videos of damage after Ukraine's attack
item.description: Ukraine struck the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, but not all the dramatic footage circulating online is real. Multiple AI-generated videos falsely show the bridge collapsed with extensive damage. Some even used branding resembling a Ukrainian news agency to appear credible. While the bridge was indeed struck and damaged, the viral videos were fabricated using AI, as Vedika Bahl explains.

item.title: Trump admin says it's weighing new penalties against China over jailed Americans
item.description: Beijing has shut down attempts to open negotiations, officials say.

item.title: Trump administration continues to insist tech outages not cyberattacks
item.description: Sec. of State Rubio also sought to assuage fears over recent outages.

item.title: Bassirou Diomaye Faye excluded from Senegal's ruling party
item.description: In tonight's edition, the political divorce between Senegal's president and the powerful former prime minister and mentor is official. Also, all of Nigeria's states have shown willingness for a push to create their own police forces. And in parts of the continent, conflict and a drop in funding have placed huge pressures on children's learning.

item.title: Muslims projected to outnumber Christians worldwide by 2035
item.description: Islam is expected to surpass Christianity as the world's largest religion by 2035, according to detailed projections released on Wednesday.

item.title: Reconstruction begins at Limoges City Hall after devastating fire
item.description: It's been a month since the nationwide protests that degenerated in violence across France. The dramatic pictures of the historic City Hall in the French city of Limoges set on fire made headlines worldwide. To the relief of many, the reconstruction work on the building has now begun. Since the fire, donations have poured in and already about 80 percent of the necessary funding has been secured. FRANCE 24's Caitlin Brown reports.

item.title: Israeli troops launch ground operation in central Gaza
item.description: Dozens of displaced Palestinians have fled their tents and shelters in central ‌Gaza after Israel launched a rare ground operation in an area it had left under a ceasefire last year.

item.title: WATCH: Man accused of starting Palisades fire faces retrial
item.description: ABC News legal analyst Brian Buckmire and correspondent Alex Stone explain what prosecutors are arguing differently and the potential sentence if the man is convicted at his federal retrial.

item.title: US Democrats nominate Jeffries to be first Black House speaker
item.description: Hakeem Jeffries is on the cusp of becoming the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives after Democrats elected him their leader Wednesday following a sweeping midterm election triumph. Jeffries faced no declared challenger, although opposition from some newly elected progressives had exposed divisions over how Democrats should wield their newfound power. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson reports from Washington.

item.title: Israeli army launches ground operation in Hamas-controlled area of Gaza
item.description: The Israeli military said it had launched an operation on Wednesday in a Hamas-controlled area of central Gaza, where an AFP journalist saw Israeli tanks position themselves east of the Nuseirat refugee camp. The rare ground operation comes after inconclusive Israeli elections, with the opposition's Gadi Eisenkot trying to form a government without caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has built his brand on saying he will ensure Israel's security. FRANCE 24's Daniel Whittington reports.

item.title: House Dems' bill would establish a 10-year expiration on final orders of removal
item.description: House Democrats told ABC News they will introduce legislation that would provide relief to some immigrants who have final orders of removal but no criminal record.

item.title: 'Netanyahu's only 2 tickets are racism or starting a war: He stopped acting as a democratic player'
item.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Israeli writer and filmmaker Etgar Keret, author of "The Seven Good Years", joining us from Tel Aviv. Keret argues that Netanyahu is seeking to remain in power, at any cost, including delegitimizing Arab parties and prolonging conflict. “For him, it could be a never-ending war as long as he's in power. He has no incentive to stop it,” he warns. Keret also calls for Israelis to examine how the war in Gaza was conducted, arguing that “the media as a whole ignored the war.”

item.title: Xi welcomes Trump: Does Nvidia scandal upend US-China AI race?
item.description: You can strike Jensen Huang from the guest list but good luck steering dinner conversation away from the topic in Shenzhen. The co-founder of the AI computing leader was to accompany the US president to the APEC summit before he was undone by revelations of a dalliance with a Chinese national that happened to coincide with a Singapore client's backdoor skirting of sanctions on its powerful H200 chips.

item.title: Anthropic share price revealed ahead of stock market debut
item.description: Demand for shares in artificial intelligence company Anthropic have surpassed expectations - signalling confidence in AI investment after a bruising fortnight for the industry.

item.title: Hochul demands information from ICE about new immigration tent facility for women
item.description: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul is demanding information from ICE and a Virginia-based construction company about a new tent immigration detention facility set to house women.

item.title: Hegseth makes surprise trip to Venezuela, renews military cooperation
item.description: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth made an unannounced visit to Caracas on Wednesday, announcing a resumption of military cooperation with Venezuela and vowing to crack down on drug traffickers. The trip marks the highest-level US visit since the ouster of Nicolas Maduro in January, signalling a dramatic shift in relations between the two countries.

item.title: William and Kate meet India's PM as they wrap up royal visit
item.description: The Prince and Princess of Wales met the prime minister of India on Wednesday to discuss trade and bilateral ‌ties at the end of their three-day visit to the country.

item.title: As overdose deaths fall, White House makes misleading claims about who deserves credit
item.description: In a statement celebrating the historic drop in drug deaths, the White House pointed to successes since President Trump took office. In fact, the biggest progress happened under the Biden administration.

item.title: Why Ukraine keeps trying to bring down Russia's bridge to Crimea
item.description: A Ukrainian drone and missile strike on Monday night brought down a stretch of the bridge linking the annexed Crimean Peninsula to Russia, potentially crippling a route long used by Moscow to move men and materiel into Crimea and the southern front. Here’s why Kyiv keeps testing its strength against an infrastructure project that has become synonymous with Russian President Vladimir Putin’s 2014 seizure of the peninsula.

item.title: Karl Kani dressed hip-hop royalty for decades. Now he's telling his own story
item.description: On NPR's Morning Edition , fashion designer Karl Kani talks about his new memoir, dressing some of hip-hop's biggest stars and why skinny jeans aren't for everyone.

item.title: Beijing has supported Moscow but 'China understands that America is way more important than Russia'
item.description: Following Xi Jinping's very friendly rare tarmac greeting for Donald Trump, Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Kerry Brown, Professor of Chinese Studies and Director of the Lau China Institute at King's College, London. Brown examines the complex relationship between the world's two largest economies, China's growing diplomatic influence and the competition over artificial intelligence.“China is the diplomatic center of the world,” says Brown, pointing to Beijing's ability to bring together leaders from Russia, the United States, Europe and elsewhere. He argues that China now has “extraordinary convening power" and significant influence over Russia.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: French ex-PM Philippe pledges to slash spending, hike retirement age as Elysée bid falters
item.description: Former prime minister Édouard Philippe pledged on Wednesday to slash public spending, scrap France’s statutory 35-hour workweek and raise the retirement age to 65 from the current 62.9 years as he unveiled a slew of measures aimed a staving off economic "catastrophe" for France. An early frontrunner in next year's presidential election, Philippe is now trailing rivals in opinion polls and at risk of missing out on the second-round runoff.

item.title: Got a canceled flight? 7 clever ways to get rebooked fast
item.description: Flying somewhere for Thanksgiving or the holidays? Travel insiders explain what to do if your flight gets canceled or delayed — so you can quickly get to your destination.

item.title: War in Ukraine: Is France in direct conflict with Russia?
item.description: An investigation published by the French public radio channel RFI on November 17 revealed that a confidential mission by the French army known as "Volia" has been used for months to conceal the presence of French personnel in Ukraine. Russia was prompt to accuse France of direct involvement in the conflict. Is this true?

item.title: Senate leadership challenge exposes divisions among Democrat
item.description: As Democrats prepare to take control of the Senate, incumbent minority leader Chuck Schumer is facing an insurgent leadership bid from Senator Chris Van Hollen and disputes over party leadership are exposing divisions over what direction to take the Democratic party after their midterms sweep.

item.title: Russia’s new low-cost munitions pose a fresh threat to Ukraine
item.description: Dan-T, Filin and Geran-5 might not mean anything to you, but in Ukraine, everyone is talking about these munitions. These new Russian weapons are small, fast and cheap – and a major threat, as they were specially designed to get around Ukrainian anti-aircraft defences and strike deep within the country.

item.title: Israel begins new military operation in Gaza
item.description: Israeli tanks advanced in an area of the central Gaza Strip on Wednesday, witnesses said, and the Israeli military said its ​forces were targeting ‌Hamas infrastructure outside the "Yellow Line" that sets the boundary of the part of the enclave controlled by Israel "The IDF launched a precise operation within the Gaza Strip earlier today west of the Yellow Line... to remove a threat posed to IDF troops operating in the Gaza Strip," the military said.

item.title: Gazans flee shelters as Israeli army launches ground operation beyond Yellow Line
item.description: Palestinians fled their tents and shelters in central Gaza on Wednesday after Israel launched a rare ground operation in an area it withdrew ​from under a ‌2025 ceasefire. The Israeli army said it crossed the Yellow Line separating Israeli and Hamas-controlled areas "to remove a threat posed to IDF troops operating in the Gaza Strip".

item.title: Democrats formally nominate Hakeem Jeffries for speaker of the House
item.description: The New York Democrat moved a step closer to becoming the first Black lawmaker in U.S. history to serve in the job, after House Democrats voted overwhelmingly to support him.

item.title: Yemen: Why the Houthis may besiege Aden rather than storm it
item.description: Bolstered by their recent military successes, Houthi rebels this week advanced close to the southern port city of Aden, the interim capital of the internationally recognised Yemeni government. Amid territorial ambitions, regional rivalries, and divisions within government forces, the potential fall of this stronghold could permanently alter the balance of power in the country.

item.title: US Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to be first Black speaker of the House
item.description: Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries on Wednesday to be the next speaker of the House of Representatives, putting him on track to make history as the nation’s first Black American with the gavel.

item.title: French presidential elections 2027: More candidates, more confusion (Episode 2)
item.description: France will head to the polls to vote for its next president in the spring of 2027. Thirty-eight candidates are currently vying to make it onto the final ballot and have until March 12 to gather backing from 500 elected officials. One figure currently stands out: Marine Le Pen. The far-right National Rally leader has a significant lead in the latest polls.

item.title: Congressional Republicans push Howard Lutnick, Jensen Huang to testify about Nvidia
item.description: Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott, a Republican, sent letters to both Huang and Lutnick to publicly testify in front of the committee

item.title: Democratic wave upends battle over Ten Commandments in Texas classrooms
item.description: Sweeping Democratic victories in the midterm elections raise questions about the future of laws mandating Ten Commandments displays in public school classrooms.

item.title: WATCH: Dog sniffs out baby's medical condition
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a mother in England whose family dog's actions helped alert her that her baby boy had a congenital heart condition.

item.title: 'It's appalling': Feds ramp up investigations of 'ghost student' fraud
item.description: Federal investigators are escalating their probe into "ghost students," digital thieves who use stolen identities to defraud the government out of student financial aid.

item.title: US loses measles-free status amid worst outbreak in 35 years
item.description: The US has lost its measles-free status after 26 years - for failing to prevent the virus spreading for more than a year.

item.title: Democrat defeats Republican in Alaska in final midterms Senate race
item.description: Democrat Mary Peltola has defeated incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan to complete a sweeping victory for the party in the Senate in the US midterm elections.

item.title: NJ sues to compel ICE facility operator to comply with subpoena in medical probe
item.description: The New Jersey AG is suing the operator of an ICE detention center for failing to comply with a subpoena issued in its probe into medical conditions at the facility.

item.title: WATCH: Eagles Autism Foundation staff shine on game day
item.description: ABC News' Will Reeve visits Lincoln Financial Field to meet neurodivergent employees helping make Philadelphia Eagles game days special through the team's commitment to autism inclusion.

item.title: Police in Philippines pursue three charges against Thomas Markle Sr
item.description: Filipino police are pursuing three charges against Thomas Markle Sr relating to child sexual abuse images, Sky News understands.

item.title: WATCH: National Geographic reveals its pictures of the year
item.description: The magazine's December issue showcases 25 of the most captivating and awe-inspiring images of 2026, selected by its editors.

item.title: Prague train crash leaves 46 people injured
item.description: Two trains have collided into each other near the main railway station in Prague, injuring 46 people.

item.title: WATCH: SUV crashes into 2 driverless taxis
item.description: Police in Phoenix are investigating what led to a multi-vehicle crash involving two Waymos as self-driving cars expand into more cities across the U.S.

item.title: WATCH: Fiona the hippo gets a super-sized tummy ache
item.description: The Cincinnati Zoo shared that its most famous resident will be getting monitored around the clock after she "ingested an object that a visitor accidentally tossed into her habitat."

item.title: UK sanctions eight firms building Israeli settlements in the West Bank
item.description: The UK has sanctioned eight firms building Israeli settlements in the West Bank.

item.title: WATCH: Pope Leo leaves Peru after historic 12-day South America trip
item.description: Pope Leo departed Peru on Monday concluding an emotional 12-day trip to South America as he recovers from cancer surgery. ABC News’ Melissa Adan reports.

item.title: WATCH: NYC teen builds candle business with refillable cement containers
item.description: What started as helping his sister make candles for a birthday party at age 13 has turned into a thriving business for New York City teen Christon Lennon.

item.title: WATCH: Meet the rental car manager going viral for keeping customers calm during ground stop
item.description: Perley Provost, manager of Enterprise Rent-A-Car at Denver International Airport, shares how he kept stranded passengers calm and hydrated during Friday's widespread ground stop.

item.title: Britain's biggest defence company to cut more than 1,000 jobs
item.description: British multinational aerospace, arms and information security company BAE Systems is to cut more than 1,000 jobs in its air division.
